# Conversation Mode

A per-session **conversation mode** for DeepSeek Harness:
the same agent, told to be a conversationa

l assistant instead of a coding agent, with coding
tools out of reach. It is a DSH bundle — a `cordi

s.patch.yml` row plus a Host plugin and a
Web client plugin — so it installs into a profile and appl
ies to every session in it.
## Install

The bundle is a DSH profile plugin. Install it into a profile the same way the other
GitHub-hosted b
undles (`dsh-frontend-review`, `dsh-git`, …) are installed:

1. **From the GitHub URL** (preferred): in the Web UI, open **Plugins → install a bundle**
and point

it at `https://github.com/stansz/dsh-convo-mode`. The plugin manager
resolves the package, adds it

to the profile, and activates it — no restart needed.
The repository is **private**, so the machine

must be signed in to GitHub as `stansz`
(for example `gh auth status` shows that account).
2. **From

a local clone**: `git clone git@github.com:stansz/dsh-convo-mode.git`, then
install that directory

as a bundle (Plugin Manager → install local bundle / the same
package-directory install the other lo

in Manager → install local bundle / the same
package-directory install the other local bundles use).

Either route mounts one row, `id: dsh-convo-mode`, name `dsh-convo-mode`.
A profile is shared by eve

ry session in it, so the mode is available in all workspaces of
that profile.
## Use

- Click the **Chat** chip at the left of the composer tool row, or type `/conversation`.
- `/convers

ation <message>` enters the mode *and* sends the message in one step.
- `/conversation off` leaves i

t; the chip toggles too.
- The mode is stored in the session log, so it survives resume, fork, and r

estarts, and it
is per session: other sessions, subagents, and teammates keep the normal coding setu

tarts, and it
is per session: other sessions, subagents, and teammates keep the normal coding setup.
## What the mode changes

1. **Prompt.** One additive system-prompt section reframes the assistant: natural prose,
length matc

hing the question, no unsolicited artifacts, one clarifying question instead
of a guess, and code on

ly as an illustration in the chat.
2. **Tools.** While active, the agent scope is restricted to a re

ad-only allow list
(`read`, `glob`, `grep`, `read_image`, web search/fetch, `ask_user_question`, `sk

ill`,
and the session-history readers). File writes, edits, shells, jobs, terminals,
delegation, and

workflow tools are not presented to the model and cannot be called.
The restriction is registered o
n that one agent and disposed when the mode leaves.
## Configure
Two equivalent surfaces:

- **Settings → Plugins → Conversation Mode → Configure** in the Web UI (the row carries a
Config sch

ema: guidance text, read-only vs unrestricted tools, the allow list, and
"start sessions in the mode

").
- A `config` override in the profile patch (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`).
Th

e row was inserted by this bundle, so it is targeted by id; `config` replaces the row's

## Implementation notes

- Durable state is the `conversation` session projection folding the logged
`command/run`/`command/d

one` pair for `/conversation`; no private session event type is
appended, so sessions stay reopenabl

e and old logs stay valid.
- The tool policy asks for the agent's own tool view (`schemas(agent)`),

because presets
compose tools onto an ancestor agent scope where the global view does not see them.

- The client half registers one chip in `conversation.input.left`; it reads the
Host-computed projec

tion and toggles by executing the same slash command.
- All styling uses `--dsw-alias-*` theme token
s; no Harness Client package is imported.
